name: Japanese Garden Impressions: 24-Pair Semantic Differential (Rokuon-ji)
description: Method replication: Wang & Kunii (2025), "Color characteristics and psychological healing effects in Rokuon-ji Temple Garden: a quantitative analysis", Frontiers in Psychology 16: 1594362. Participants see ten photographs of the Rokuon-ji (Kinkaku-ji) garden in Kyoto, drawn at random from 22 openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photos along the visitor path (pond, golden pavilion views, moss garden, paths, stone arrangements), and rate each on the paper's 24 semantic differential pairs from Table 4 (opened-enclosed, peaceful-disturbing, natural-artificial, restorative-draining, spiritual-secular and others) on a 5-point scale. Pair order is random and about half of the pairs are shown reversed, as in the paper; answers are stored with 5 = positive word. Then age, gender and familiarity with Japanese gardens. Analysis as in the paper: factor analysis of the 24 pairs (the paper found Openness, Decorativeness, Clarity, Naturalness, Unity, Complexity), clustering of photos on factor scores, and correlation with colour metrics of each photo. Photographer and licence are shown under each photo. Differences from the original study: (1) the authors' 42 photos are not released (the paper prints one), so 22 Commons photos from different seasons and photographers replace them, without the pilot healing-quality selection; (2) ten photos per participant instead of all 42; (3) online instead of a calibrated-display lab; (4) the garden-familiarity item is our own wording.
author: Wang & Kunii
